fac_engineering.talk: The Faculty of Engineering gives every student a shared preparatory year, then three specializations: mechatronics and automation, AI and machine learning, and energy and electrical power, with construction engineering also on offer. Learning is hands-on from the start, with robotics projects and training at the Suez Canal Authority Training Center. Our AI students also train through the Huawei ICT Academy hosted at EPNU. The programs are led by two directors with UK doctorates. Dr. El-Sakka, who also heads our International Relations Office, has published widely on wind energy, including highly cited work on vertical-axis turbines. Dr. Rady, a Newton-Mosharafa scholar, works on solar and thermal management of photovoltaics.
caveats: El-Sakka's Sheffield PhD is a probable match only: it rests on an OpenAlex/ORCID profile for "Mohamed M. Elsakka" at Port Said University. The middle name "Metwally" appears on no academic profile. Say "reported" or "according to public records", not "verified".
Dr. Rady's identity is better supported (PSU staff page, Google Scholar and the EPNU Engineering page agree on the Exeter PhD).
Some EPNU news posts give directors' titles as Assistant Professor; the slide uses the titles the university confirmed, so do not improvise a different rank aloud.
Program duration and credit hours are not published consistently: a 165 credit-hour figure appears on the site but the study plan is marked "to be updated soon". Do not quote it.
The Energy & Electrical Power specialization has no named director on the slide; do not name one.
fac_engineering.likely_question: How many credit hours and years is the engineering degree?
fac_engineering.suggested_answer: The program follows a preparatory year plus a specialization, but the final study plan and credit-hour total are still being updated on our website. We will send you the approved regulations in writing.

fac_cs.talk: The Faculty of Computer Science and IT offers four-year programs in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science in information systems, and biomedical informatics. The last one is distinctive: it applies computing to clinical data, biometrics and medical imaging. Our students are active in competitive programming and qualified for the Egyptian Collegiate Programming Contest in 2026. The faculty is led by Professor Osama El-Baksawy, who also directs our Quality Assurance Center. His own research is in renewable energy and fractional-order control, and one of his IEEE Access papers has more than a hundred citations. We have also begun cooperation talks with ITI on digital-skills training.
caveats: El-Baksawy's rank is inconsistent in EPNU sources: the Arabic faculty heading says Professor, but his own biography text and several news posts say Assistant Professor. The slide uses the title the university confirmed; verify before printing it on formal documents.
His PhD institution and year were not found, so do not mention his doctorate. His field is electrical power engineering, adjacent to rather than inside computer science.
His metrics (24 papers, about 780 citations, h-index 15) are auto-generated by OpenAlex and may be incomplete. One 2023 paper lists a different affiliation, which is unresolved.
ITI and Creativa are described as cooperation talks only. No signed agreement was found.
Credit hours for all four programs are not published ("to be updated soon").
fac_cs.likely_question: Do you have a formal agreement with ITI?
fac_cs.suggested_answer: We have held cooperation meetings on digital-skills training, and we are happy to say more once there is a signed document. At this stage we describe it as talks.

fac_medicine.talk: Our Faculty of Medicine offers an integrated, English-medium MBBCh: five years over ten semesters, followed by a two-year internship. Basic sciences, clinical training and community service are taught together, and the ECTS credit system makes it familiar to European partners. Students join medical convoys to primary-care units in North Sinai, and they present research at national conferences. The program director, Dr. Sherine El-Khouly, holds a GAHAR professional diploma with an Excellent grade, from the first cohort of Egypt's healthcare accreditation authority. Clinical training runs through partner hospitals, including Port Said University's new hospital, Ahl Masr Hospital and the 57357 children's cancer hospital.
caveats: Internal only: Egyptian media in August to October 2026 reported a dispute over the size of the Medicine intake. See extra_findings.md section A1. Figures vary by source and the official reasons were not published. Do not raise it unprompted; if asked, use the neutral line below.
Do not promise Medicine places, exchange numbers or a teaching-hospital opening date. Clinical training is through partner hospitals; no EPNU teaching hospital details are public.

Dr. El-Khouly's home institution, specialty and publication record were not found, so avoid describing her specialty. Her rank appears as Assistant Professor in some Arabic posts; the slide follows the confirmed title.
The credit-hour total is not published; only the ECTS system is named.
The 57357 item is an MoU and Ahl Masr a signed protocol; do not upgrade either to a joint program.
fac_medicine.likely_question: How many Medicine students do you admit each year?
fac_medicine.suggested_answer: Medicine intake follows the capacity limits set by the Supreme Council of Private Universities and the readiness of our clinical-training sites. We would rather confirm the current figure in writing than quote a number from memory.

fac_pharmacy.talk: The Faculty of Pharmacy offers a Bachelor of Pharmacy, PharmD in Clinical Pharmacy, over ten semesters in English. Students use HPLC and UV-Vis instruments, and clinical simulation rooms where they practice dose calculation. The faculty has industry partners including EIPICO, EVA Pharma, Lavender Life and Royal Cosmetics. It is also where our first international partnership began, with Universiti Putra Malaysia, including joint webinars. Pharmacy and medicinal chemistry produce most of our international publications; our most-cited papers are on triazole-based anticancer candidates. The program is directed by Dr. Mohamed Yasser, who also runs the Entrepreneurship Club and lectures on innovation in pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulation.
caveats: Dr. Yasser's rank: some EPNU posts say Assistant Professor (for example post 2751); the slide uses the confirmed title Associate Professor.
No publication profile was found for him (OpenAlex, Scholar, ORCID). The research credit belongs to the faculty's staff generally, not to him personally.
The UPM relationship is the only foreign MoU found; do not describe it as a joint degree or exchange program.
The list of six scientific departments is marked provisional on the website. Credit hours and internship length are not published.
The research claim ("most of our international papers") is based on automatic field labels and affiliation matching; see the research slide notes.
fac_pharmacy.likely_question: Is the PharmD accredited, and is there an internship year?
fac_pharmacy.suggested_answer: The program is approved within Egypt's national-university framework. We have not published accreditation details or an internship structure online, so we will send you the official study plan once it is final.

fac_ahs.talk: The Faculty of Applied Health Sciences Technology trains the technologists behind modern diagnostics, in two programs: Medical Laboratory Technology and Medical Imaging and Radiologic Technology. Teaching is in English, with 131 credit hours. Students work in hematology, biochemistry, microbiology and microscopy labs, and train on X-ray, CT and MRI equipment with an emphasis on radiation protection and quality. Practical training takes place across a hospital network: Port Said University Hospital, Saudi German Hospital in Cairo, Ahl Masr Hospital and the 57357 Group, with which we have signed an MoU. The faculty is directed by Dr. Salma Khairallah, a biochemist who holds her PhD from Port Said University.
caveats: The 131 credit hours is stated on the faculty page but is not confirmed as specific to each program; say "about 131" if challenged.
Dr. Khairallah is titled Prof. Dr. on the faculty page but Dr. in news posts; use Dr. as instructed. Her specialty is biochemistry, not radiology, so do not present her as an imaging expert.
No publication record was found for her, and her current permanent post is not independently verified.
Program durations are not published. The clinical-training partners also include Bahia Hospital and a plasma donation center, but those are not on the slide.
fac_ahs.likely_question: Do graduates receive any international recognition?
fac_ahs.suggested_answer: We have not yet published any international recognition for these programs. What we can offer today is hospital-based training with named partners, and we would welcome discussion of joint curriculum or exchange.

fac_business.talk: The Faculty of Business Sciences prepares graduates for a digital economy through two programs: Accounting and Software Applications, and Digital Marketing and E-Management. On the accounting side, students work with accounting information systems, financial software and financial analysis. On the marketing side, they learn campaigns, e-commerce, platform management and consumer analytics. This is one of our newest faculties, and it welcomed its first cohort with a dedicated orientation day. Dr. Ali Gomaa leads the Accounting program, which points graduates to careers in accounting, auditing, taxation, banking and financial software. We see good scope for exchange and joint teaching in digital business.
caveats: Dr. Gomaa's role at EPNU rests on a single Facebook post (the first-cohort orientation); it is not on the website. His home institution, qualifications and research could not be verified. Do not say where he previously worked or what his doctorate is in.
He is not the former Grand Mufti of the same name; avoid any confusion.
The Digital Marketing program has no named director on the slide.
Duration, credit hours and vision/mission statements are not published for this faculty.
Some EPNU news posts give directors' titles as Assistant Professor; the slide uses the titles the university confirmed, so do not improvise a different rank aloud.
fac_business.suggested_answer: I do not have his full academic profile in front of me, so I would rather not guess. We will send you a short biography from the faculty after this meeting.

fac_arts.talk: The Faculty of Arts pairs the humanities with technology. English Language and Translation covers written and interpreting translation, including medical, legal, literary and audiovisual work, plus applied linguistics for media, tourism and diplomacy. Geomatics and Artificial Intelligence is quite unusual in an arts faculty: it covers GIS, remote sensing, digital surveying, cartography and AI-based spatial analysis, with graduates aiming at urban planning, smart cities and telecoms. For international partners this is a natural fit for joint work in translation studies, digital humanities and smart-city research. Given our location at the Suez Canal, geospatial skills are directly relevant to regional planning.
caveats: No program director is named for this faculty on the slide because none was confirmed; if asked who leads it, say we will provide the contact.
The faculty has no published vision or mission, and no program duration or credit hours; the website says information will be added soon.
The "natural partner" line and the Suez Canal remark are our own analysis, not claims from the website. Present them as opinion.
No joint program with any foreign university in these fields is documented; do not imply one exists.
fac_arts.likely_question: Is the translation program accredited by any international body?
fac_arts.suggested_answer: We have not published an international accreditation for it. The strength we can describe is the specialized translation tracks and the link to technology, and we would welcome a conversation about collaboration.

research.talk: Research is where a young university can show momentum. Since 2024, more than eighty peer-reviewed papers and chapters carry the EPNU affiliation: seven in 2024, thirty-eight in 2025, and thirty-six so far in 2026. Ninety-eight percent appear with international publishers, led by Elsevier with twenty-seven papers and Springer Nature with twenty. About two-thirds have co-authors abroad, from fifteen countries, mostly in the Arab region. The strongest areas are medicinal chemistry and pharmacy, medicine, and renewable energy. Our most cited paper so far, nineteen citations, studies triazole compounds that target cancer pathways. We think the true total is higher than we can show today.
caveats: The count is 81, found by matching raw affiliation text in OpenAlex, Crossref and Europe PMC. It is NOT verified as Scopus- or Web of Science-indexed, and OpenAlex has no institution record for EPNU. Say "81 publications identified in open databases", never "81 Scopus papers".
A paper qualifies with any one EPNU-affiliated co-author, so many may be mainly Port Said University work with EPNU as a secondary affiliation. This could overstate the output.
The count may also be too low (indexing lag, truncated or misspelled affiliations, staff who publish only under their home university).
Roughly 100 affiliation strings for the separate East Port Said University of Technology were excluded; do not confuse the two institutions.
The 15 countries and 63 percent international co-authorship are lower bounds. Most collaboration is with Arab-region institutions; Western partnerships are few, so do not imply otherwise.
Publication counts do not mean the faculty directors authored these papers; only some directors have profiles.

Independent cross-check: a PubMed affiliation search for 'East Port Said National University' returns 56 records (about 54 articles; biomedical only). The only figure the university itself has published is 23 pharmacy papers for 2024-25 (post 4806), so cite '80+' as our own bibliometric count, not as an official university statistic.
research.likely_question: Are these papers indexed in Scopus, and in which quartiles?
research.suggested_answer: Most of the journals are from publishers such as Elsevier, Springer Nature, RSC and Wiley, which are widely indexed. We identified the papers through open databases and have not yet checked Scopus or quartile rankings, so we prefer not to claim them. We can share the full list.
